name: Truck Art
basis: why: covered in flat enamel colour, painted flowers and outlines; how: nine enamel colours, flat regions, black outlines, chrome bands, floral frame
note: The brief's own example; chamak patti and chrome are garnish.

lumenary.blurb: The painted lorries of Pakistan: flat, loud colour, heavy black outlines, a gloss of chrome light and a frame of flowers and chains.

facts.era: Flourishing since the mid twentieth century

why: A Pakistani truck is a moving canvas. It is covered from bumper to roof in flat enamel colour, painted flowers, birds and poetry, and a frame of chains and rosettes, with strips of shiny reflective tape (chamak patti) that glitter in headlights. Every part is made by a specialist: the painter, the woodcarver and the metalworker. Nothing is left plain, because the truck is the driver’s home, pride and calling card.
how: Blur the picture (radius = simplify × 1.2 px) and raise its saturation by half.
Give each pixel the nearest of nine enamel colours, using the redmean distance, which weights red, green and blue the way the eye does.
Run a majority filter over a 5 by 5 window twice so regions are flat, as brush-painted ones are.
Draw a black outline wherever the colour index changes and grow it by up to 2 px, then cross the brightest places (tone above 0.74) with diagonal bands of white, like chrome.
Wrap everything in a frame as wide as 11 percent of the shorter side, with a red rim, a yellow field of flowers and leaves, a row of pearls and a twelve-petal rosette in each corner.
history: Decorating lorries, buses and rickshaws grew with the long-distance road trade of the twentieth century, drawing on Mughal and Persian ornament and on local styles such as Peshawar’s carved wooden fittings and Karachi’s painted panels. Painters often learn as apprentices and work in small workshops. Truck art has been shown in museums and festivals abroad, and a new generation of artists now paints on canvas, walls and buildings as well.
terms: Shiny reflective tape used to decorate trucks.
A formula that measures colour difference more like the eye does than plain RGB distance.
paragraphs: Pakistani truck art covers a lorry from bumper to roof in flat enamel colour, painted flowers, birds, poetry and a frame of chains and rosettes, with strips of shiny reflective tape (chamak patti) that glitter in headlights. Every part is made by a specialist: the painter, the woodcarver and the metalworker. The program keeps the look in four steps: reduce the picture to a few loud colours, outline them in black, add glints, and wrap everything in a frame.

Colour reduction first. The picture is blurred (radius = simplify × 1.2 px) and its saturation is raised by half. Each pixel then takes the nearest of nine enamel colours, using a distance that weights red, green and blue the way the eye does (the “redmean” formula below). A majority filter over a 5 × 5 window, run twice, removes specks so that regions are flat, as brush-painted ones are. A black outline is drawn wherever the colour index changes and is then grown by up to 2 px. The brightest places (tone above 0.74) are crossed by diagonal bands of white light, like chrome. The frame, as wide as 11% of the shorter side, has a red outer rim, a yellow field with a row of flowers and leaves, a row of pearls and a corner rosette of twelve petals.

equations.tex: d^2=\Big(2+\frac{\bar r}{256}\Big)\Delta r^2+4\,\Delta g^2+\Big(2+\frac{255-\bar r}{256}\Big)\Delta b^2,\qquad \bar r=\frac{r_1+r_2}{2}
equations.note: The “redmean” colour distance used to find the nearest enamel colour. It is a cheap approximation of how different two colours look.
Outline width w and strength e from the outline slider o (0 to 1).
Chrome gloss added to the colour: s is the gloss slider and t the tone. The two levels make bands of light.
Frame width, with φ the frame slider (0 to 1). Below 6 px the frame is dropped.

presets.text: The Peshawar palette is hot and high contrast.
Heavy outlines and strong simplification look like fresh enamel.
A wide frame turns the whole picture into a truck panel.
